goal: Expose the `Strategy` Protocol from `docs/strategy.md` plus a no-op default implementation, leaving concrete branch/PR strategies deferred.

constraints: Protocol shape matches `docs/strategy.md` exactly: `setup(task) -> StrategyContext`, `submit(ctx) -> StrategyResult`, `cleanup(ctx) -> None`.
The no-op default must satisfy the Protocol without performing any git, filesystem, or network side effects — it returns the typed context/result shells and exits.
The strategy module remains pure data + Protocol: no `subprocess`, no `git`, no network. Concrete implementations land in later, dedicated work.
`StrategyContext` and `StrategyResult` are typed (dataclasses or equivalent) so concrete implementations cannot diverge on the wire shape later.
non_goals: Concrete branch/PR/merge strategies (deferred per `docs/strategy.md` Status section).

Branch slug derivation beyond exposing the `derive_slug(commit)` helper hook described in `docs/strategy.md` — the implementation can be a minimal stable function, but rich conventional-commit parsing is out of scope.
Wiring the strategy into the harness flow (harness already runs without it in `roadmap-10-harness`).
edge_cases: Calling `cleanup` after a `setup` that no-op'd must be safe — it does not assume any state was created.
A `submit` on the no-op default returns a deterministic, typed result (e.g. with an empty `ref`) so callers do not need to special-case `None`.
`derive_slug` on an empty or whitespace-only commit message produces a stable fallback rather than raising — its contract is total.

assertions: The Strategy Protocol, StrategyContext, StrategyResult, and a no-op default implementation are exposed from `flywheel`, matching `docs/strategy.md`.
The no-op default satisfies the Protocol without git, filesystem, or network side effects, and tests demonstrate this directly.
`derive_slug(commit)` is exposed as documented and has total behavior — empty/whitespace input does not raise.
The strategy module imports no `subprocess`, `git`, or network APIs.
graders.name: strategy-protocol-contract
